_readme: W-0203 / P1.2. The full worker pipeline, switched on against deterministic fakes.
Everything this file turns on is a loop the worker ships DISABLED, and shipping them
disabled is correct: a stack somebody starts in order to look at it must not dial anything.
The cost was that every rehearsal of the pipeline re-derived the switch-on configuration by
hand, so what actually ran was a wall of environment variables in a shell nobody kept. This
file is that configuration, written down once, diffable, and citable from an evidence pack.
What it deliberately does NOT relax: ExecutionMode stays MOCK, SimProvider stays MOCK and
RealCustomerCallAllowed stays NO. MockSchedulerDispatchGateway.IsReady requires all three, so
this profile cannot reach a vendor even if one were configured. The kill switch is the only
safety lifted, and it is lifted against a fake gateway every one of whose destinations is the
same allowlisted fake string. The profile also refuses to load outside a non-production
environment; see IvrConfigurationProfile.
Ivr:Scheduler:CallingWindow is left ENABLED and widened to the whole day rather than switched
off. The hour gate is a safety control: a rehearsal that disables it stops exercising the code
that decides, and a rehearsal whose result depends on what time it was started is not a
rehearsal. 0..1440 keeps the decision running and always open.
Ivr:Retention is armed and is NOT a dry run, because a retention loop that only reports is not
the loop the pipeline has to survive. RetentionJobHost runs ONE pass per worker start, which is
how a CronJob invokes it, so every worker restart in a rehearsal is also a retention pass.
The periods are 365 days, and that number is a blast-radius decision rather than a policy one:
the real periods are still OWNER/Legal input (P5). A rehearsal shares the developer database
with whatever else is in it, and a short period would make every worker restart delete other
people's rows as a side effect. At 365 days nothing any current environment holds is eligible,
so the harness proves deletion the only honest way left - it back-dates its OWN cohort past the
period, restarts a worker, and asks for those rows back.
Ivr:Telephony:Mock:Scenarios keys ending in '*' match by task-id prefix (W-0203). The gateway
is a singleton built once from this snapshot, so before prefixes existed a scenario could only
be scripted for an identifier already known at process start - which meant a hundred-round
loop had to restart the worker between rounds, and restarting the worker between rounds
destroys the crash-recovery signal the loop exists to measure. Longest prefix wins.
